A Bluetooth headset\'s or car\'s voice button, and a wired or USB headset\'s long press, open Robot. Robot never takes your play and pause buttons and holds no media session, so your music app keeps them; it resumes after Robot answers. During a phone call the button does nothing to the call.\n\nWith the headset\'s microphone, Robot uses the headset as for a call while it listens and answers, and lets go right after. Personal answers play only in headphones you said only you can hear: wired and USB headsets are, a Bluetooth headset once you say so, a car or a speaker never. If the headset goes, Robot stops at once. Device names stay on this phone and never enter the voice log.

Car mode is Robot\'s own hands-free mode over your car\'s Bluetooth, not Android Auto. When your car connects, Robot says “Car mode on”, talks through the car, and shows big buttons. Press your car\'s voice button or say “hey robot”, then “navigate home”, “call Mom” or “what\'s next”. Answers are short. Everything else works as it does outside the car: Robot doesn\'t hold or refuse anything because you\'re driving, since a passenger may be the one asking.\n\nCalls open the dialer unless you choose to call after a spoken yes; emergency numbers always open the dialer, and Robot never calls one itself. Navigation opens your maps app\'s route preview, where you tap Start. Places are kept on this phone only: type or paste coordinates (in your maps app: a place › Copy coordinates), or use where you are now.
Such as 45.50170, -73.56730 (in your maps app: a place › Copy coordinates). Empty: none.
Turn the car on and let the phone connect to it, then come back
